title: cairnmap reads a roster the corpus retired
intention: cairnmap reads a roster the corpus retired
why: cairnmap IS the diagnostic surface for charter coverage, and it is currently reporting 15 errors that do not exist while the real fault — its roster reader is stale — is invisible. A gate that cries wolf stops being read, and this one has not been read for weeks. Law 7: errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces. A false red is the inverse hollow of a false green, and it costs the same thing: a peer stops leaning on the surface.
how: cairnmap.py:134 reads `.get('members_so_far', [])` — an ABSENT key returns the default rather than an error, so `roster_err` stays None, the guard at line 237 lets both roster lanes run against an empty roster, and 15 chartered skills red as 'missing from the roster'. But members_so_far was retired on purpose: node_classes/skill.json now carries `members_derived_by` ('ls -d ~/dev/src/cairn/skills/*/ | grep -v __pycache__') and CairnCommons/node_classes/proofs/test_membership_derived.py asserts members_so_far must be ABSENT. Two candidate fixes, and the choice is the design question: (a) minimal and faithful — a missing key is an unreadable roster, one finding, both lanes ABSENT, exactly clause 12; (b) follow the retirement — derive membership from members_derived_by. Note (b) makes the charter-vs-roster comparison tautological (the roster becomes the set of skill dirs), so the lane's original purpose — catching the set's own record forgetting its newest members — is discharged by the derivation itself, and the lane should become a check that members_derived_by is present and its command still resolves.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth. cairnmap IS the diagnostic surface, and it is currently reporting 15 errors that do not exist while the real fault (its roster reader is stale) is invisible. Also Law 8: a gate that manufactures findings is the inverse hollow — not a false green but a false red, and a peer leaned on a surface that cries wolf stops reading it.
falsifier: DONE when (1) `cairnmap --gate` over the live corpus reports the roster fault ONCE if at all, never once per skill; (2) the retirement proof and cairnmap agree about where membership lives; and (3) the gate's remaining findings are all real. WRONG INTENT if the fix is to put members_so_far back — that would red CairnCommons/node_classes/proofs/test_membership_derived.py::test_members_so_far_removed and re-open a defect the corpus already closed on purpose. (The three clauses were MARKED, not written, on 2026-09-11: the sentence already enumerated them with semicolons, and proof_coverage.clauses() reads `(N)` markers, so the unmarked form collapsed to the single fallback clause "all" and admitted exactly one declared tooth. `cairn test --hollow` counts declared teeth only, so this component's charter and its WATCHME probe both read HOLLOW — not because nothing checked them, but because nothing could be declared to. Marking changes what can be DECLARED, never what is promised.)

in: cairn/tools/cairnmap/cairnmap.py — the roster reader at line 134 and the guard at line 237
cairn/tools/cairnmap/proofs/test_cairnmap.py — the fixtures encoding the retired field, plus a NEW tooth for the missing-KEY shape
cairn/tools/cairnmap/intention+why.json — only if the design shifts (the falsifier clause already states the rule; it likely does not need touching)
out: The other 6 real findings in the same gate run: /ruled carrying a charter but not installed in ~/.claude/skills, and the 5 bin/cmd entries (groundloop, mailcheck, operator, review, ruled) no charter's invoke names. Real, but different work in different components — tidying them in would make the gate green for two reasons at once.

CairnCommons/node_classes/proofs/test_membership_derived.py's missing __main__ block and its failing derivation-count tooth — that is the live trouble proofs-with-no-main-block-seal-green-over-zero-teeth.
Restoring members_so_far in any form. It reds an existing commons proof and re-opens a closed decision.
